body.text: How many weeks of hospital stay and physiotherapy are required before flying?

Inpatient hospital stays for knee or hip arthroplasty and routine spine decompression typically run three to five nights, followed by one to three weeks of local outpatient physiotherapy before flying. However, long-haul flights carry deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risks, so only your operating surgeon can clear your exact departure date.

Clinical guidance from the [Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS](https://roh.nhs.uk/services-information/other-info/before-surgery/travel-surgery-and-dvt) advises avoiding flights longer than four hours for at least four weeks after general surgery and waiting up to three months after hip or knee replacement where possible. Similarly, [Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS](https://www.nnuh.nhs.uk/publication/download/surgery-travel-and-deep-vein-thrombosis-8/) notes that blood-clot risk rises sharply on journeys exceeding four hours, while [OrthoInfo by the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS)](https://www.orthoinfo.org/globalassets/pdfs/after-your-joint-replacement-surgery.pdf) emphasizes structured clot prevention and early mobilization. Because every patient's procedure, mobility, and anticoagulation plan differs, book flexible return tickets rather than fixed low-cost fares.

body.text: Which physical therapy and accessible hotel arrangements are needed?

Post-operative orthopedic stays require a true step-free room with a roll-in shower, firm high-seat chairs, elevator access, and proximity to your hospital or licensed physiotherapy clinic. Standard boutique hotels in historic Istanbul districts often have narrow stairs, deep bathtubs, and steep cobblestones that make crutches or walkers unsafe.

Before confirming accommodation, verify room measurements and door widths rather than relying on generic "accessible" filter tags. [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism) is an independent, client-paid, flat-fee advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions—so we vet hotels and ground transfers strictly around recovery practicality. You can also confirm a hospital's international safety standing using [Acıbadem's guide to verifying JCI accreditation](https://acibademinternational.com/patient-guides/how-to-verify-hospital-accreditation-in-turkey/) or reviewing institutions such as [Memorial's JCI quality framework](https://www.memorial.com.tr/en/corporate/qualit-management-system).

body.text: How do you book business-class or extra-legroom flights for orthopedic recovery?

Reserve extra-legroom bulkhead seats or lie-flat business-class cabins on refundable or changeable fares, and register airport mobility assistance at least 48 hours before departure. Note that emergency exit rows are prohibited for passengers using crutches, casts, or wheelchair assistance, so bulkhead or business cabins are the practical choice.

Through [Turkish Airlines Special Assistance](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/any-questions/special-assistance-for-passengers/) and its [Wheelchair Assistance program](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-kw/any-questions/special-assistance-for-passengers/wheelchair-assistance/), passengers with reduced mobility can request complimentary terminal-to-gate wheelchair support, dedicated check-in, and priority boarding. Ask your airline whether a MEDIF medical clearance form is required for recent orthopedic surgery, and carry your surgeon's written fit-to-fly letter plus prescribed anticoagulants in hand luggage.
What discharge imaging and implant documentation must you bring home?

Before leaving your hospital in Türkiye, collect your full English discharge summary, operative report, post-operative X-rays or CT scans in DICOM format, and your official implant identification card. Your home orthopedic surgeon and physiotherapist need these exact records for follow-up imaging, staple removal, and long-term joint monitoring.

As outlined in [AAOS Total Knee Replacement guidance](https://www.orthoinfo.org/bodypart/kneelower-leg/total-knee-replacement/), joint prostheses contain metal components that may trigger airport security detectors, making an implant card useful alongside standard screening. Store digital copies on an encrypted USB drive and carry printed originals in your cabin bag.

faq.q: How soon can I fly after knee or hip replacement in Türkiye?
faq.a: Your operating surgeon decides when you are fit to fly based on wound healing, mobility, and blood-clot risk. Many short-haul patients depart after two to three weeks with medical clearance, while long-haul flights over four hours often require longer waiting windows.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye choose my orthopedic surgeon or hospital?
faq.a: No. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. We organize independent logistics—vetted accessible hotels, private transfers, companion arrangements, and scheduling support—without taking commissions from hospitals or clinics.

faq.q: Can I book an emergency exit row for extra legroom after surgery?
faq.a: No. Airlines prohibit passengers with reduced mobility, casts, braces, or crutches from sitting in emergency exit rows. Choose a non-exit bulkhead seat or a lie-flat business-class seat instead.

faq.q: What if my recovery takes longer than planned?
faq.a: Book changeable return flights and hotels with flexible extension terms. If your surgeon advises extra days of wound care or physiotherapy, you can adjust your stay without penalty shock.

faq.q: Should I bring a travel companion for spine or joint surgery?
faq.a: Yes. Having a companion helps with luggage, medication reminders, meal runs, and airport navigation during the first two weeks after orthopedic surgery.

faq.q: What records does my home physiotherapist need?
faq.a: Bring your English operative note, post-op weight-bearing protocol, range-of-motion targets, medication list, and DICOM imaging files so your local therapist can continue rehabilitation safely.
